Writing the circle fiber as a rotation composed with (z+ε)/(1+εz), the product's normalized half-trace is [cos(2π(c+μ q_j sin α))+ε² cos(2πμ s_j cos α)]/(1−ε²). Thus the positive-trace component about zero drift is |c+μ q_j sin α|<h_j; the one-step analog uses h_0. The lower bound (2/5)cos(π/10)/π>1/10 puts zero strictly inside all three intervals. At the positive endpoint the trace crosses transversely, with derivative proportional to −sin(2πh_j) for the two-step returns; their off-diagonal term contains cos(πd_+)≠0 in the stated strip, and the one-step off-diagonal is always nonzero. These are genuine nonidentity parabolics, not identity resonances. The bound on h_j′ makes c_2−c_1 strictly increasing across the open strip, with opposite signs at −π/2 and zero. The difference c_1−c_0 is negative on the nonpositive half and strictly increases on the positive half, where its sign changes. The possible c_2=c_0 tie is not an envelope switch: on the positive half c_1<c_2. The uniform expansion h_j=h_0−ε π μ²s_j² cos²α/(2√(1−ε²))+O(μ⁴) gives roots of order μ. Using (s_1²−s_2²)/(q_1−q_2)=1/2 and s_1²/(1−q_1)=1+q_1 yields the stated coefficients and cubic remainders.
